messages:
sarah_support: Heads-up — multiple customers (tenant IDs: 9876, 1122) reporting p95/p99 spikes (~3-8s P95, 12-18s P99) for text generation since ~09:10 UTC. Also seeing intermittent 401s from the API gateway for dedicated pools.

eli_sre: Saw the alert. Is this only Dedicated?
sarah_support: Yes, only Dedicated pools. Hosted API routes look normal. Customers say it started after a big marketing burst around 09:05.

tony_oncall: I pulled traces from the request logs. Pattern: incoming request -> attach attempt -> auth call to token service -> attach timeout -> 500 upstream returned to customer. When attach succeeds later, response times are huge.

eli_sre: Can someone paste a snippet of the attach logs?
sarah_support: paste below:
```
attach-service: start attach pool=dedicated-eu-985 tenant=9876 req=abc123
auth-client: POST /token verify -> 429 rate_limit exceeded (retry-after=3)
attach-service: attach worker init failed: auth: token fetch error
attach-service: backoff and retry (attempt 3) -> timeout 10s
pool-proxy: upstream timeout -> 504
```

mike_platform: Interesting — the auth-client is hitting rate limits on our internal token service. That would explain 401/429s and delayed attach. Looks correlated with massive burst of attach attempts.

eli_sre: Do we have metrics on attach concurrency vs token issuance rate?
mike_platform: Yes, we have a per-tenant attach rate cap, but the autoscaler launched many parallel attach flows because queue depth jumped. Token service has a per-service client QPS cap that we exceeded when many attach processes tried to refresh credentials at once.

tony_oncall: So root cause: scale-up cold-attaches trigger many token fetches -> auth service throttles -> attach processes stall -> requests pile up -> p99 spikes and 401/429 for some flows. Also dedicated pool saturation made autoscaler more aggressive.

sarah_support: Customers are formatting urgent tickets. Any immediate mitigations we can do from support side?

eli_sre: Short term options:
- Enable fallback routing to Hosted for affected tenants (transparent to app) — requires approval but fastest mitigation.
- Manually prewarm a small reserved pool for top customers (quick but capacity limited).
- Increase token-service client quota for attach-service (requires infra change, could be rolled quickly with caution).

mike_platform: I can increase the token-service client quota for attach-service to reduce throttling, but we should throttle attach concurrency and add jitter at the autoscaler to prevent recurrence.

tony_oncall: Action items then:
1) mike_platform: temporarily bump token-service quota for attach-service by 2x — will monitor. (ETA 15m)
2) eli_sre: add randomized jitter and sliding window limit on attach concurrency in autoscaler config (can ship a config change to prod as a roll-forward). (ETA 2h)
3) sarah_support: offer affected customers a Hosted fallback and manual prewarm; open incident tickets and note mitigation.
4) infra-bot: create incident with severity P2 and link traces + tenant IDs.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-4587. Linked traces and sample logs.

sarah_support: Update from customer 9876: accepted Hosted fallback, will failover at 09:50 if we give them a connection string.

mike_platform: Increased token-service quota; auth 429s dropped immediately in metrics. Still seeing some attach timeouts as workers recover. Monitoring p95/p99 now.

eli_sre: Rolling a config patch to autoscaler: add exponential backoff + per-attach jitter (0-250ms) and cap parallel attach to 6 per-pool by default. Pushing to canary right now.

mike_platform: FYI, we also found attach code re-fetches token on cold-start repeatedly instead of sharing cached token across attach goroutines. I'll patch to share fetch where safe. (ETA 4h for canary).

tony_oncall: Good. For the runbook we should add:
- Detect: sudden spike in attach attempts + token 429s + p99 latency + 401s
- Mitigate: bump token quota, enable hosted fallback, prewarm pool, apply autoscaler cap/jitter
- Long term: change token fetch sharing, add attach queue smoothing, telemetry alert on token 429 rate

sarah_support: I updated customer tickets and posted the Hosted fallback string. Customers 9876 and 1122 confirmed improved latency after failover. Remaining customers are being offered prewarm.

eli_sre: Canary of autoscaler patch looks good on EU canary cluster — attach rates steadied and no auth 429s under simulated burst. Scheduling gradual rollout.

mike_platform: Deployed token-fetch sharing patch to canary; memory/cpu impact minimal. Planning a prod rollout after autoscaler rollout.

tony_oncall: Closing loop: please add post-incident notes to INC-2026-4587 with root cause = attach-induced auth throttling + aggressive autoscale concurrency; mitigations performed; next steps for infra and platform.

sarah_support: Thanks everyone. I'll follow up on the tickets and mark customers as monitored. :thumbsup:

eli_sre: Assigning follow-ups to backlog: AUTO-549 (attach jitter + cap), AUTO-550 (attach token sharing), OBS-312 (alert on token 429 spike).

mike_platform: Monitoring for 2h; will revert token quota if stable.

tony_oncall: Great work. Reopen thread if anything else pops up.
